tested_scope: Constructed role-local scheduled-Chat switch TX-5 at scope S1 only, with four fixed restart points and fixed duplicate/scope/transport/conflict controls. This is recovery-logic conformance, not a database benchmark.

public_sources.name: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
public_sources.bound_semantics: The original state is preserved while changes are appended to a separate log, and a commit occurs when a special commit record is appended.

public_sources.name: SQLite WAL-mode file format recovery
public_sources.bound_semantics: Restart recovery scans the durable log and identifies the last valid commit frame, so incomplete tail state is not treated as a committed state.

public_sources.name: PostgreSQL write-ahead log documentation
public_sources.bound_semantics: WAL retains information required for crash recovery, and durable commit behavior is tied to WAL records being flushed before recovery can rely on them.

source_binding_limit: Only the durable-record-before-finalization distinction and restart recovery from durable records are imported. SQLite/PostgreSQL runtimes, databases, servers, filesystems, hosted workflow engines, and any external recovery service are not part of the accepted Chat-native execution route.

candidate_results.reason: Writing B into the authority pointer before durable qualification/finalization makes the externally visible authority itself an ambiguous intent record and permits pre-finalization authority transfer after interruption.

success_and_restart_trace: PREPARED is sealed/read back with A still authoritative.
QUALIFIED is sealed from distinct same-scope terminal evidence; A remains authoritative.
FINALIZED_DECISION is sealed/read back only after qualification passes; A still remains authoritative until the separate pointer update succeeds.
A compare-and-set authority update from recorded A to B is attempted only after finalized-decision readback; a mismatch against C is a conflict and is not forced.

Restart after PREPARED resumes qualification; restart after QUALIFIED resumes from persisted qualification; restart after FINALIZED_DECISION replays only the idempotent pointer update; restart after pointer=B closes bookkeeping without second credit.
failure_and_controls: Qualification failure seals ABORTED/REJECTED and leaves A authoritative; a stale late TX-5 promotion is rejected.
Duplicate qualification, scope mismatch, and transport timeout do not advance semantic state.
Pointer changed to C causes compare-and-set conflict and prevents stale authority transfer.

candidate_results.reason: Rerunning the whole switch after every restart discards durable progress identity and permits duplicate qualification, authority transfer, and credit, violating G6-G9.
An external hosted workflow/recovery runtime is a residual execution dependency and may rely on finite optional quota or paid capacity.

accepted_claim: For the exact TX-5 fixed trace, separating durable intent, qualification, finalized decision, and authority pointer transfer makes restart behavior unambiguous: no pre-finalization interruption transfers authority, committed-but-not-applied transfer is replayable, already-applied transfer is idempotent, and stale/conflicting completions fail closed.
not_claimed: No claim of full database atomicity/durability semantics, production crash safety, or general optimizer superiority.
exact_next_action_after_readback: Advance controller credit by one only after independent readback. Then precommit a distinct sequential evidence-accumulation switch test before reading any public source for that next leaf.
